title: Ignored Error Leading to Fail-Open Authorization
platform_conditions: Go 1.x standard library; applies to all build targets
security_mechanism: Go surfaces failures as values, and the zero value of a bool/struct is indistinguishable in syntax from a legitimate result. Discarding err with _ (or shadowing it with := in an inner scope) leaves the zero value in the variable that the security decision then consumes: verifyToken's (valid, err) becomes valid=false on error, but the same pattern with an inverted convention (err-only helpers returning a session struct) yields an empty-but-non-nil value that downstream code treats as authenticated. Error shadowing across a function boundary means a later assignment can overwrite the failure before it is checked, so the review must trace the specific variable instance.

source_sink_clues.source: Authentication, signature verification, certificate validation, and permission-check calls whose error results are discarded or shadowed.
source_sink_clues.sink: valid, _ := verifyToken(token); err := ... with := re-declaration shadowing an outer err; if err == nil checks placed after the variable was reassigned; authorization flows that treat a zero-value session or claims struct as valid

tracking_guards: Check the specific failure path: on verification error the code must return/deny, not fall through to a zero value; check for := shadowing of err inside if/for blocks whose scope reaches the security decision; check that errors are compared with errors.Is/!= nil before any use of the paired result.
not_candidate_when: Every error from the verification call is checked with != nil and the handler returns before using the result, the discarded error comes from a call whose failure cannot affect the decision (e.g. closing an already-closed resource on a non-security path), or the shadowed variable is a distinct local that never feeds the authorization outcome.
synthetic_safe_example: valid, err := verifyToken(token); if err != nil || !valid { return false }; grantAccess()
public_references: CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html
